events.text: Case opened: Death at the Meridian Observatory

At 23:40 on Saturday night, security guard Nell Okafor found the observatory's director, Dr. Elias Voss (58), dead on the floor of the main dome beneath the telescope gantry. The donor gala had been running in the hall next door since 19:00. Voss was last seen leaving the hall at about 22:25. First responders assumed a fall on the gantry stairs. Three people had reason to quarrel with him that night: his deputy director Dr. Mara Quill, his doctoral student Theo Lark, and board chairman and principal donor Gideon Ashby. The dome corridor camera was not recording. Whether this is an accident or a homicide — and who, if anyone, should answer for it — is for the investigation to establish.
Set out how I intend to run this.

Somebody in that building is behind the death of Dr. Elias Voss, and I've got three names: Dr. Mara Quill, Theo Lark, Gideon Ashby. I'll walk the scene, then I want them in a room one at a time while their stories are still warm. People crack before paperwork does.
Flag the easy assumption.

Before anyone says "fall", let me read the floor. A stumble and a shove write completely different geometry — where he landed, how far out, what he was holding. Get me the scene untouched, his clothes, his hands, and anything electronic. The body will tell us which story is true.
Tell the team what a charge needs.

For a charge I need three things pointing at one person: a motive, the opportunity, and something physical that ties them to that gantry. A quarrel is not a case. And if you go into anyone's private space, you bring me a warrant first — I will not lose an exhibit to a suppression motion.

Members of the jury, the question is not whether Dr. Mara Quill could have done this. It is whether the prosecution has made you sure. The fingerprints on the gantry rail: theo operates the telescope from that gantry most nights. Fingerprints cannot be dated. The voss's mobile phone: the Ashby text does not say what 'this' refers to, and the draft email was never sent. The gala photographs: people take shawls off indoors; the photographs show nothing of the dome. Meanwhile the evidence about Theo Lark — his are the only identifiable prints on the rail Voss went over — was never answered. If you have to squint to see guilt, that squint is reasonable doubt. Not guilty.

Dr. Mara Quill pushed Elias Voss over the upper gantry rail at about 22:50. Over three years she had diverted 240,000 of grant money to a shell company registered to her sister-in-law. Voss found the hole in the accounts, told her on Saturday afternoon that he would lay it before the board on Monday, and went up to the dome after the speeches. She had already switched off the corridor camera. She left the archive room, let herself into the dome with her override card, and asked him for time. He refused. In the struggle on the gantry he tore the fringe of her shawl; she pushed him. She buried the shawl in the archive bin and was back in the hall for the 23:20 group photograph.
